quick_skim.title: One Frozen Simulator Is Not Enough: Simulator Collapse in Multi-Agent RL
quick_skim.abstract: Multi-agent reinforcement learning for human-AI interaction typically relies on a single large language model to simulate user behavior. We show that this approach systematically fails to generalize, and trace the failure to simulator collapse: because the simulator LLM is mode-collapsed, an LLM policy trained against it overfits to narrow strategies that exploit the simulator's dominant mode, and such a policy transfers poorly to unseen simulators and real users. We formalize this collapse theoretically and propose two complementary solutions, one at inference time and one at training time. The inference-time solution, Verbalized Sampling, broadens the simulator's behavior by sampling from a verbalized response distribution, reducing mode collapse. The training-time solution, Co-Training, jointly optimizes the policy against a population of trainable simulators, preventing it from overfitting to any single simulator's mode. We validate both solutions on three multi-turn benchmarks: Persuasion for Good, $τ^2$-bench, and CooperBench. Verbalized Sampling improves held-out success by up to 9% over single-simulator RL, and Co-Training pushes gains further to 14%; the human study shows similar gain on real users. Both solutions preserve the policy diversity that collapses under single-simulator RL. To support further work in this direction, we release SCOPE, an open-source framework for Population Co-Training multi-agent RL. More broadly, our results suggest that the diversity of the training environment, not only the policy, is critical to the generalization of multi-turn RL to real-world deployment.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: The paper shows training multi-agent RL policies against a single LLM simulator leads to overfitting and poor generalization due to simulator mode collapse. It proposes Verbalized Sampling at inference and a training-time solution to broaden simulator behavior. This method is valuable for training game AI bots that must generalize beyond simulated opponents or users.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 基于单一LLM模拟器的多智能体强化学习存在模拟器坍缩问题，训练出的策略过拟合模拟器主导模式，在新模拟器或真实用户上表现差。本文形式化模拟器坍缩，提出推理端言语化采样扩大模拟器行为分布，并补充训练端方案降低模式坍缩。实验证明该方法能减少策略对模拟器狭窄策略的利用，提升迁移鲁棒性。该研究成果为使用模拟器训练游戏AI智能体等交互策略提供了泛化保障。
